semantically_equivalent_domains.justification: Multi-robot systems involve the coordination and operation of multiple robots acting together, which is semantically equivalent to multi-agent systems, where multiple agents (robots, in this case) work collaboratively.

parent_domains.justification: Robotic systems is a broad category that encompasses various types of systems involving robotics, including multi-robot systems.
Robotics is an overarching domain that includes all aspects of robot design and application, including multi-robot systems.
Autonomous systems include any systems that can operate independently, and multi-robot systems often function in an autonomous capacity.
Collaborative robots focus on robots working together, which aligns with the concept of multi-robot systems.

closest_parent_domain.justification: Robotic systems is the closest parent domain as it directly encompasses systems involving robots, including the multi-robot configuration.

child_domains.justification: Collaborative robots focus more specifically on the interaction and cooperation aspect within multi-robot systems.
This area is specialized within multi-robot systems focusing on how multi-robot systems can learn to collaborate and interact through reinforcement learning.

closest_child_domain.justification: Collaborative robots are the direct application of multi-robot systems with an emphasis on cooperation between robots.

sibling_domains.justification: Autonomous vehicle systems, like multi-robot systems, are a subset of autonomous systems but focused specifically on vehicles.
Robotic manipulation deals with a specific aspect of robotic function and operation, parallel to the function-coordination focus of multi-robot systems.

closest_sibling_domain.justification: Autonomous vehicle systems share the closest relationship in terms of system coordination and autonomous operation characteristics with multi-robot systems.

unrelated_domains.justification: Robot photography is generally focused on capturing images and does not relate directly to the coordination and operation concepts of multi-robot systems.
While important for efficiency, energy management does not specifically pertain to the multi-agent or multi-robot coordination aspects of the Given Domain.
Bipedal robots refer to a specific type of robot design and do not directly relate to multi-robot coordination.
This domain focuses on interaction between humans and robots, which is not necessarily related to the multiple robot coordination aspect of multi-robot systems.
Robot exploration focuses on the exploration goals of robots, which isn't specific to the multi-robot systems coordination and interaction.
